companion_hired: Right then. Where you go, I go, so long as the coin comes at dawn.

companion_hired.text: Coin first, then the road. That's how I like it.
Good. I was getting soft sitting about {settlement}.
I'll come. Don't expect me to like the rain.
An adventure! Wait till I tell my mother.
By the old gods, a road at last.
The mountain taught me patience. You'll teach me the rest.

companion_wait.text: I'll keep watch till you're back.
Here? Fine. I'll count the crows.

companion_dismissed: Home it is. Remember me if you need a hand again.

companion_dismissed.text: Fair enough. The coin was good while it lasted.
Safe roads to you. I'll tell them at {settlement} what we saw.
Home. My own bed. Thank the saints.

companion_fight.text: I've broken worse at the gate.

companion_hurt.text: This was not in the bargain.
I need to sit a moment.

companion_road: Good weather for walking, at least.

companion_road.text: My feet are complaining. I'm ignoring them.
Smell that? Pine and rain. Best smell there is.
Keep an eye on the treeline. Bands like the woods.
Every mile's a mile's wage. I'm counting.
I heard a story about this road once. Ends badly. Never mind.
The fields here are poorer than ours.
Flat country. I miss the peaks.
Wind's off the sea. It'll rain by noon.
Not a well in sight. Drink sparing.
Moor's as wide as the sky out here.

companion_night.text: I don't like the dark out here.
Night's when the honest folk sleep and the rest of us work.
Stars are out. My grandmother named every one.
We should find a fire. Or make one.

companion_place.text: Look at that roof. We've nothing like it at home.
Their ale had better be good.
I wonder what they say about us here.
Keep your hand off your sword. They don't know us.
Better market than ours. Don't tell anyone in {settlement}.

companion_home.text: Ah, the smell of my mother's kitchen from here.
Back in {settlement}. Everyone will want to hear the stories.
Home. Don't let me get comfortable.

companion_deed.text: I'm proud to walk with you.
Worth every bit you pay me. More, maybe.
I'll tell it at the tavern. With a few more of them.

companion_crime: I didn't see that. I don't want to have seen that.

companion_crime.text: That's not how we do things.
Not my business. Not my town.
If that were my town, we'd be done, you and I.

servant_greet: You're back! The house kept well.

servant_greet.text: Welcome home. The fire's lit and the larder's full.
Oh! You're home. Mind the floor, it's wet.
Home at last. I'll tell you everything.
